name: Learn: RBAC & Certificates
description: Master Kubernetes authorization step by step — Roles, ClusterRoles, bindings, ServiceAccounts, least-privilege, and approving a CSR. Then prove it in the cka-006 exam.
objective: CKA › Cluster Architecture, Installation & Configuration (25%). Goal: create Roles/ClusterRoles and bindings, grant ServiceAccounts, scope least-privilege with resourceNames, and approve a CSR — RBAC & cert tasks that appear on almost every CKA.

questions.title: Role + RoleBinding (namespaced)
questions.teach:
**RBAC** decides who can do what. A **Role** lists allowed *verbs* on *resources* within one namespace; a **RoleBinding** grants that Role to a subject (here, user `dev`). Build both with `kubectl create role` / `kubectl create rolebinding`.

**Gotcha:** both objects must exist — a Role alone grants nothing until a RoleBinding points a subject at it.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `rbac-learn`, create a Role `pod-reader` allowing `get,list,watch` on `pods`, and a RoleBinding granting it to user `dev`.

Target: `kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=dev -n rbac-learn` → `yes`.
questions.hint: `kubectl create role pod-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods -n rbac-learn`, then `kubectl create rolebinding dev-pr --role=pod-reader --user=dev -n rbac-learn`.
questions.solution:
kubectl create role pod-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods -n rbac-learn
kubectl create rolebinding dev-pr --role=pod-reader --user=dev -n rbac-learn
kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=dev -n rbac-learn   # -> yes

verification.description: user 'dev' can list pods in rbac-learn

questions.title: ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding (cluster-scoped)
questions.teach:
Cluster-scoped resources like **nodes** live outside any namespace, so a namespaced Role can't reach them. Use a **ClusterRole** for the rules and a **ClusterRoleBinding** to grant them cluster-wide: `kubectl create clusterrole` then `kubectl create clusterrolebinding`.

**Gotcha:** check cluster-scoped access with no `-n` flag — `kubectl auth can-i list nodes --as=dev`.
questions.prompt:
Create a ClusterRole `node-reader` allowing `get,list` on `nodes`, and a ClusterRoleBinding granting it to user `dev`.

Target: `kubectl auth can-i list nodes --as=dev` → `yes`.
questions.hint: `kubectl create clusterrole node-reader --verb=get,list --resource=nodes`, then `kubectl create clusterrolebinding dev-nr --clusterrole=node-reader --user=dev`.
questions.solution:
kubectl create clusterrole node-reader --verb=get,list --resource=nodes
kubectl create clusterrolebinding dev-nr --clusterrole=node-reader --user=dev
kubectl auth can-i list nodes --as=dev   # -> yes

questions.title: ServiceAccount identity
questions.teach:
**ServiceAccounts** are identities for workloads, not humans. You grant one permissions the same way — bind a Role to it with a RoleBinding. The CLI shortcut uses a colon: `--serviceaccount=<ns>:<name>`.

**Gotcha:** in `auth can-i --as=` the SA is the full form `system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<name>`, not the short `ns:name` used on the binding.
questions.prompt:
In `rbac-learn`, create a ServiceAccount `ci`, then bind the existing `pod-reader` Role to it with a RoleBinding.

Target: `kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:rbac-learn:ci -n rbac-learn` → `yes`.
questions.hint: `kubectl create sa ci -n rbac-learn`, then `kubectl create rolebinding ci-pr --role=pod-reader --serviceaccount=rbac-learn:ci -n rbac-learn`.
questions.solution:
kubectl create sa ci -n rbac-learn
kubectl create rolebinding ci-pr --role=pod-reader --serviceaccount=rbac-learn:ci -n rbac-learn
kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:rbac-learn:ci -n rbac-learn   # -> yes

verification.description: ServiceAccount ci can list pods in rbac-learn

questions.title: Least privilege with resourceNames
questions.teach:
Least privilege can go below resource level: `resourceNames` restricts a rule to **specific named objects** — e.g. `get` only `app-config`, not every ConfigMap. CLI: `--resource-name=app-config` (repeatable).

**Gotcha:** `resourceNames` only works for verbs targeting a named object (`get`, `update`, `patch`, `delete`) — it can't restrict `list`, `watch`, or `create`.
questions.prompt:
Two ConfigMaps exist in `rbac-learn`: `app-config` and `other-config`. Create a Role + RoleBinding so user `dev` can `get` **only** `app-config`.

Target: `can-i get configmaps/app-config --as=dev` → `yes`, but `can-i get configmaps/other-config --as=dev` → `no`.
questions.hint: `kubectl create role cm-reader --verb=get --resource=configmaps --resource-name=app-config -n rbac-learn`, then bind it to `dev`.
questions.solution:
kubectl create role cm-reader --verb=get --resource=configmaps --resource-name=app-config -n rbac-learn
kubectl create rolebinding dev-cm --role=cm-reader --user=dev -n rbac-learn
kubectl auth can-i get configmaps/app-config  --as=dev -n rbac-learn   # -> yes
kubectl auth can-i get configmaps/other-config --as=dev -n rbac-learn   # -> no

verification.description: dev can get app-config but NOT other-config

questions.title: Approve a CertificateSigningRequest
questions.teach:
A **CertificateSigningRequest** lets an admin issue a client cert to a new user. List pending ones with `kubectl get csr`, then grant one with `kubectl certificate approve <name>`; its condition then reads `Approved,Issued`.

**Gotcha:** approval only proves identity — it grants no permissions without a binding.

The CSR `learn-dev` is already submitted and **Pending** — approve it.
questions.prompt:
Approve the pending CSR named `learn-dev`.

Target: `kubectl get csr learn-dev` shows condition `Approved,Issued`.
questions.hint: `kubectl get csr` to see it Pending, then `kubectl certificate approve learn-dev`.
questions.solution:
kubectl get csr
kubectl certificate approve learn-dev
kubectl get csr learn-dev   # Approved,Issued
